title: Internet and AI
description: Understand the internet, browse and search safely, use email, protect your privacy, and learn how to use AI wisely.

blocks.text: The Internet is a huge network that connects computers and other devices around the world.
These connections allow people to: Send emails, Communicate, Search for information, Watch videos, Play games, Learn, Shop, Make payments, Share files
The Internet connects people and information from many different places.
Many devices can connect to the Internet.
Examples: Laptop, Desktop computer, Smartphone, Tablet, Game console, Smart TV, Smartwatch
Look around your home or classroom. Find five devices that can connect to the Internet.Write them down:
These two words are often confused.
🌐 Internet: The Internet is the worldwide network.
📶 Wi-Fi: Wi-Fi is a way for your device to connect to a network without using a cable.
A network is a group of connected devices. For example: 💻 ─── 💻
The Internet is a very large network of networks.
A website is a collection of related web pages available on the Internet. For example, a school might have a website containing: Home, Courses, Teachers, Contact. Each page is part of the website.
A web page is one page that you can view in a web browser. For example: a website might contain: Home page, Courses page, Teachers page, and Contact page
A web browser is a program used to access websites. Common browsers include: Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Safari, Microsoft Edge …
You use a browser to visit websites.
Look at the computer you are using. Which browser are you using?
A search engine helps you find information on the Internet.Examples include: Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo
You type something you want to find.For example: weather in Kigali. The search engine finds pages related to your search.
A browser is the program you use to access the Internet. A search engine helps you find information. For example:
You can open Google using Chrome.
A URL is the address of a page or resource on the Internet.
For example: https://www.example.com. Think of a URL like a street address.
A URL tells the browser where to go.
A link is something you can click to go to another page or website.For example: 🔗 Learn More
When you click it, the browser opens another page. Links can contain:Text, Images, Buttons
Open a website. Find three links. Write what each link says.
A server is a computer that provides information or services to other computers.
For example, when you open a website, your browser requests information from a server.
The server sends information back to your device.
ISP means:Internet Service Provider. An ISP is a company that provides Internet access like MTN, Mango. For example, your home or school may get Internet access from an ISP.
The basic idea is:🏠 Your home 📶 Router 🏢 ISP 🌐 Internet
A router helps connect devices to a network. For example: Laptop, Phone, Smart TV can connect to: Router
The router connects them to the network and, when configured for Internet access, to the Internet.
You do not always need Wi-Fi to access the Internet. A smartphone can use: Mobile data
Mobile data is provided through a mobile network.
Decide which connection is being used.
You connect your laptop to your home wireless network. ______________
You turn off Wi-Fi on your phone and browse the Internet using your SIM card._______________________________________________________
The Internet can be very useful.
📚 Education: Students can find learning materials.
💬 Communication: People can communicate across countries.
💼 Jobs: People can work and find jobs online.
🛍️ Business: Businesses can sell products online.
🌍 Information: People can learn about places and cultures around the world.
🦹 Scams: Some people try to trick others.
🔐 Privacy problems: Sharing too much information can be dangerous.
😡 Cyberbullying: People can use the Internet to hurt others.
❌ False information: Not everything online is true.
⏰ Too much screen time: Spending too much time online can affect other activities.

1. What Does It Mean to Be Connected?

In Lesson 1, you learned that the Internet is a worldwide network of connected computers and devices. But your computer or phone needs a way to join that network. When your device can communicate with other devices and services on the Internet, we say: Your device is connected to the Internet.For example:

📱 Phone → Internet
💻 Laptop → Internet
🖥️ Desktop computer → Internet
📺 Smart TV → Internet
🎮 Game console → Internet

2. How Does Your Device Reach the Internet?
Think about travelling to another city. You go from : Your house → Road → Main road → Other places
The Internet works in a similar way: Your device → Network connection → Internet → Website or online service
Your device does not simply "jump" directly to every website. It uses networks and equipment that help information travel from one place to another.
Wi-Fi is one of the most common ways to connect devices to a network without using a cable.
For example, at home you may have:
The router provides a Wi-Fi network that nearby devices can join.
TRY IT: Find Wi-Fi and Connect to it
If you have a phone, tablet, or computer:
Step 2: Look for Wi-Fi or Network & Internet
Step 4: Look at the available Wi-Fi networks.

Step 6: Check whether it says: Connected

Another way to connect to the Internet is mobile data. Mobile data allows a phone or another device to access the Internet through a mobile network.
Mobile networks are provided by companies called mobile network operators.
MTN, Airtel, and other operators depending on your country.
Both can connect you to the Internet, but they work differently.

Often used at home, school, or offices

A router is a device that helps connect devices to a network and directs network traffic.You might see a router with several lights and antennas.
Think of a router as a traffic controller. It helps information travel to the correct device.
ISP means: Internet Service Provider. An ISP is a company or organization that provides Internet access.For example, MTN Rwanda, Canal Box, Liquid telecom.

Find a browser on your computer.
Look at the top of the window.
Type the name of a website.
A URL is the address of something available on the Web. For example: https://www.example.com
A URL can tell the browser where to find a webpage.
Look at the address bar when you visit a website. Write down one URL:
A link, or hyperlink, allows you to move from one webpage or online resource to another.
Move your mouse over a link. The pointer may change shape. Click the link and observe where it takes you.
You do not need to open a completely new browser window every time you want another website. You can use tabs.
Back ↩️ : Returns to the previous webpage.
Forward ↪️: Moves forward after using Back.

1. Can We Trust Everything Online? => No.
Anyone can publish information online.A webpage may contain:

✅ Correct information
❌ Incorrect information
⚠️ Old information
⚠️ Opinions presented as facts
⚠️ Misleading information
This is why Internet users must learn to check information.
Look for: Author, Organization, School, Government, University, or Expert
Be careful when there is no clear source.
Information can become old. For example, an article about: Technology, Sports, Prices, Science, or Current events may become outdated.
Look for the publication or update date.
Suppose one website says: The answer is 50. Do not immediately assume it is correct.Search for the same information elsewhere.
If reliable sources agree, you have stronger evidence.
Clickbait is content designed mainly to make people click.
You won a Million francs, click to collect!!!
A dramatic title does not automatically mean the information is true.

☐ Who wrote it?
☐ When was it published?
☐ What evidence is provided?
☐ Can another reliable source confirm it?
You can find millions of images online. You can search for: Animals, Maps, People, Places, Science diagrams or Buildings
Search for: volcano diagram Open several images. Compare them.
Video websites allow people to watch educational and entertainment content.
Search for: water cycle for children Choose an educational video.
While watching, write down three things you learned.
Online maps allow you to explore places. Try searching for: Kigali Rwanda
Find: Roads, Schools, Hospitals, Parks, or Important buildings
Do not share your home address publicly.

lessons.title: Email and Creating a Gmail Account

blocks.text: Email is a way of sending and receiving messages using the Internet.An email can contain: Text, Pictures or Documents
An email address tells an email service where to send a message. An email address usually looks like:student@gmail.com
If your teacher or parent has approved the creation of a Gmail account, follow the instructions they provide on the Google account sign-up page.
Open your web browser. For example: Chrome
Step 3: Choose to create an account
Look for: Create account, your teacher or parent will tell you which account type to choose.
Enter the name requested during account setup. Use your real information where Google requires it, and follow your parent/teacher's instructions.
You will need to choose an available Gmail address. For example: myname@gmail.com
Your chosen address must be available. If someone already has that address, Gmail will ask you to choose another one.
A password protects your account. Choose a strong password according to your teacher/parent's guidance.
Never tell your classmates your password.
Do not write your password where other students can see it.
During account setup, Google may ask for recovery information.
This can help you regain access if you forget your password.
A parent or guardian may help with this.
For a classroom account, follow your teacher's instructions.
Do not use another person's phone number or email for account recovery without their permission.
Google accounts have age requirements, and the rules can depend on the country.
If Google says that you are too young to create or manage an account yourself:
STOP and ask your teacher or parent for help.
Do not enter a false age just to create an account.
Your teacher or parent can help choose the correct account option.
Once your account has been created:
Step 3: Select Sign in if necessary.
Your Inbox contains emails that other people have sent to you.
An unread email may appear differently from an email you have already opened.
Compose means creating a new email. Look for Compose Click it. A new email window will appear. You will normally see:
The To field contains the email address of the person who should receive the message. For example: To: teacher@example.com
If you type the wrong email address, your message may go to the wrong person.Always check the address before sending.
The Subject tells the receiver what your email is about. A good subject is short and clear.
Examples: My Internet Homework, Science Project, Question About Homework
The message is where you write what you want to say. A simple school email might look like:
I have completed my Internet homework.

✅ Be polite.
✅ Use complete sentences.
✅ Check your spelling.
✅ Say what you need clearly.
This is my first practice email.
I am learning how to use Gmail.
Your email will travel through the Internet to the recipient.
Your teacher may reply to your email.
If someone sends you an email, you can Reply.
Reply means sending a response to the person who sent the message.
Open the email from your teacher. Click: Reply
An attachment is a file included with an email. For example: Word document, Excel spreadsheet, Picture, PDF
Create a simple text document called: My Internet Lesson. Write three things you learned and save the file.
Wait for the file to finish attaching.
Check that the file appears in the email.
Your teacher may send you a file. When you receive it:
Download it only if it is expected and safe.
Find the downloaded file on your computer.
Do not open unexpected attachments. For example, you might receive: Congratulations!!!.exe from someone you do not know.
Sometimes you may need to delete a message. Practice with a teacher-approved practice email.

Phishing is when someone tries to trick you into giving away information or clicking something dangerous. For example: "Your Gmail account will be deleted today! Click this link immediately!" This is suspicious.

🚩 Urgent language
🚩 Strange links
🚩 Requests for passwords
🚩 Requests for private information
🚩 Unexpected prizes
🚩 Messages pretending to be someone else
If you receive a suspicious email:

❌ Click suspicious links.
❌ Give away your password.
❌ Send personal information.
❌ Download unknown attachments.
❌ Reply to the sender.

✅ Stop.
✅ Show the message to a teacher or trusted adult.
✅ Report it if instructed.
✅ Delete it when appropriate.
Click this link NOW and enter your Gmail
Does this look suspicious? Yes / No
Should you give the sender your password? Yes / No
Remember: Your password is a secret, not a message.
If someone asks for your password: STOP and ask a trusted adult.

Phishing is an attempt to trick someone into giving away information or doing something unsafe.
A message might say: "Your account will be deleted today! Click this link immediately!"

🚩 Asks for a password

Message A: Your teacher has uploaded today's homework to the school learning platform.
Message B: CONGRATULATIONS!!! You won $10,000! Send us your password now!!!
Which one is suspicious? And Why?
Cyberbullying is bullying that happens using digital technology. It may involve: Insults, Threats, Humiliation, Spreading rumours, Sharing embarrassing content, Excluding someone deliberately
If someone is bullying you online:
Step 1: Do not respond with more bullying.
Step 3: Block or report the person when possible.
Step 5: If someone is in immediate danger, seek help from a responsible adult or appropriate emergency service.
Work with a partner. One student receives a suspicious message.
The other student explains what to do. Practice saying:
"I won't click the link.", "I will show this to a trusted adult."
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is technology that allows computers to perform tasks that normally require human-like abilities.
AI assistants allow people to communicate with an AI using natural language.
You can ask an AI: Explain photosynthesis for a 10-year-old and the AI will generate an answer.
AI does not automatically know that every answer it produces is correct.

❌ Give incorrect facts
❌ Misunderstand questions
❌ Produce outdated information
❌ Invent information
❌ Give answers that sound confident but are wrong
Search for the answer using reliable sources.
Jupiter is the largest planet in our Solar System.
This is why AI should be a helper, not the only source of truth.
A prompt is the instruction or question you give an AI.
Better: Give me five interesting facts about lions for a 10-year-old.
Even better: Explain five interesting facts about lions using simple English.
Give each fact in one short sentence.
Ask an AI:Explain why the sky is blue for a 10-year-old. Read the answer.
Now search for the same topic using a search engine. Compare:
Write one thing they agree about.

But you should not simply copy AI answers and pretend you created the work yourself.
Use AI to learn, not to avoid learning.
